```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Use `oauth_db_dremio()` to query a Dremio Flight SQL endpoint with each
visitor's OAuth access token. The helper returns a DBI connection through
adbi and Apache Arrow's ADBC Flight SQL driver. Dremio checks the token and
applies the visitor's database permissions.

This guide uses Dremio Enterprise's direct external JWT authentication.
Your administrator must configure an external token provider that trusts
the JWT access tokens issued to the Shiny app. Signing in to Dremio's web
console does not configure this integration.

## Install the driver

The app below installs the R packages if needed. Use adbcdrivermanager 0.25.0 or later. The R packages do not include the
Flight SQL shared library. Follow Apache Arrow's
[driver installation instructions](https://arrow.apache.org/adbc/current/driver/installation.html).
With the `dbc` driver manager installed, run:

```sh
dbc install flightsql
```

The helper's default `driver = "flightsql"` selects that installed driver.
Alternatively, pass the full path to the ADBC Flight SQL shared library
as `driver`. An ODBC driver or JDBC JAR cannot be used here.

## Configure sign-in and database access

Ask the Dremio administrator to configure an
[external token provider](https://docs.dremio.com/current/security/authentication/)
with the issuer, expected audience, signing keys and claim that identifies
the Dremio user. The user must exist in Dremio and have permission to query
the requested data. Configure TLS on the Flight SQL endpoint as well.

Register the Shiny app with that provider using the
[app registration instructions](getting-started.html#register-your-app).
Request a JWT **access token** intended for Dremio. The audience and scopes
depend on your deployment; `database.read` below is an example scope that
your provider must define or replace.

Save these settings in the app's `.Renviron` file and restart R:

```text
OAUTHDB_DREMIO_ISSUER=https://login.example.org/realms/reporting
OAUTHDB_DREMIO_HOST=dremio.example.org
OAUTHDB_DREMIO_SCOPE=database.read
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID=your-client-id
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET=your-client-secret
```

The provider must issue the correct audience. Providers that require an
explicit audience parameter can use
`extra_auth_params = list(audience = "your-dremio-audience")` in the
discovery call below. For Entra, configure a shinyOAuth token target for
the resource registered by your Dremio administrator; the built-in SQL
Server target is a different resource.

## A complete Shiny app

The app shows the Dremio user for the current connection. Replace the
query with a query against a table the user can access. Use fully qualified
table paths when the query needs a specific source or schema.

After signing in,
click **Load rows**. The app starts its workers once and stops them at shutdown.

```{r app}
pkgs <- c("shiny", "shinyOAuth", "shinyOAuthDB", "mirai", "adbi", "adbcdrivermanager")
for (pkg in pkgs) {
  if (!requireNamespace(pkg, quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages(pkg)
  }
}

library(shiny)
library(shinyOAuth)
library(shinyOAuthDB)

provider <- oauth_provider_oidc_discover(
  issuer = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_DREMIO_ISSUER")
)

client <- oauth_client(
  provider,
  client_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID"),
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8100",
  scopes = c("openid", "profile", Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_DREMIO_SCOPE"))
)

ui <- oauth_ui(
  fluidPage(
    actionButton("login", "Sign in"),
    actionButton("logout", "Sign out"),
    actionButton("load", "Load rows"),
    tableOutput("rows")
  ),
  id = "auth",
  client = client
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  auth <- oauth_module_server(
    "auth",
    client,
    auto_redirect = FALSE,
    async = TRUE
  )
  observeEvent(input$login, auth$request_login())
  observeEvent(input$logout, auth$logout())
  con <- oauth_db_dremio(
    auth$connection,
    host = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_DREMIO_HOST")
  )
  query_task <- oauth_db_task(con)
  observeEvent(input$load, {
    query_task$invoke("SELECT CURRENT_USER AS database_user")
  })
  output$rows <- renderTable(query_task$result())
}

runApp(
  shinyApp(ui, server, uiPattern = ".*", onStart = function() {
    mirai::daemons(2)
    onStop(function() mirai::daemons(0))
  }),
  port = 8100,
  launch.browser = FALSE
)

# Open the app in your regular browser at its registered redirect URI.
```

Open `http://localhost:8100` in your regular browser. Sign in with an account
mapped to a Dremio user. If authentication succeeds but the query fails,
check the token provider's audience and user claim, database grants and
network access from the Shiny server.

## Connection options and results

The default port is `32010`; pass `port = 443` if your Flight SQL endpoint
uses that port. For private certificate authorities, pass the path to a
PEM certificate file with `ca_bundle`. The helper requires TLS and verifies
the server certificate and hostname.

Use `bigint = "character"` to return 64-bit integers as strings. Other
result conversions follow adbi. DBI's Arrow methods can return Arrow
results without converting them to a data frame. The `timeout` argument
sets a timeout for each connection, query, fetch or update RPC; it does
not impose one deadline on a whole query.

Call `con()` before each operation. It replaces the connection when its
access token changes, and closes outstanding results on replacement.
Finish fetching results before requesting another connection. Reopening
also loses connection state, including an explicitly selected SQL context.
Ordinary token renewal does not rerun a completed reactive query.

The driver holds a fixed bearer during each DBI operation. Renewing the
Shiny token does not update a query or fetch already in progress. A query
that outlives its credential can fail; choose `min_valid_for` to allow
enough remaining lifetime for the operations your app performs.

Sign-out, account changes, permission loss and session end close the local
connection. A saved native handle may retain copied credentials until it
is closed. A submitted server job can continue after the client closes;
the helper does not cancel server jobs or replay failed queries.

## Token exchange and Cloud editions

Dremio Enterprise documents direct external JWT authentication for Flight
SQL clients. `oauth_db_dremio()` sends the visitor's access token directly;
it can also send a Dremio OAuth token already acquired by shinyOAuth.
It does not call Dremio's `/oauth/token` exchange endpoint or start the
ADBC driver's own OAuth flow. A named shinyOAuth target selects a token
already managed by shinyOAuth and does not perform that exchange.

[Dremio Cloud Classic's external-token guide](https://docs.dremio.com/cloud/security/authentication/app-authentication/external-token/)
documents a different connection recipe using a password and
`token_type=jwt`. That recipe does not establish compatibility with this
Flight SQL bearer path. Verify the authentication requirements of your
Cloud edition and endpoint before using this helper. There is no automatic
fallback to a PAT, service user or hosting account.

The package tests credential isolation, token replacement and connection
cleanup. A local TLS Flight SQL fixture checks the real ADBC transport.
Live Dremio Enterprise issuer mapping, permissions and Cloud compatibility
still require validation against a configured deployment.
